inspiration.observed_pattern: A MySQL/MariaDB schema migration adds a named foreign-key constraint with ON DELETE CASCADE after the tables already exist.
inspiration.mysql_mariadb_translation: Reauthored as a shipment manifest migration. An existing manifest_items table receives a named foreign key after its tables and valid rows are created; deleting a manifest then cascades only its items while preserving items for other manifests. The source schema, names, values, and application purpose are new.

fixture_notes: Manifest 7001 has two items and manifest 7002 has one. Adding the foreign key succeeds with existing valid rows; deleting manifest 7001 removes only its items, leaving manifest 7002 and its item.
determinism_notes: All manifest and item IDs are fixed and final reads use primary-key ordering. No clocks, randomness, sleeps, or concurrent connections are used.
setup: CREATE TABLE shipping_manifests (manifest_id INT PRIMARY KEY, destination_code VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL)
CREATE TABLE manifest_items (item_id INT PRIMARY KEY, manifest_id INT NOT NULL, package_code VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL)

steps.sql: ALTER TABLE manifest_items ADD CONSTRAINT fk_manifest_items_manifest FOREIGN KEY (manifest_id) REFERENCES shipping_manifests (manifest_id) ON DELETE CASCADE

checks.sql: SELECT manifest_id, destination_code FROM shipping_manifests ORDER BY manifest_id
SELECT item_id, manifest_id, package_code FROM manifest_items ORDER BY item_id
